about.summary: Glafira is a desktop Apache Kafka client for testers and developers. Connect to clusters over PLAINTEXT, SASL or mTLS, browse topics and consumer groups, search messages, send them one at a time or in batches from a file, reset offsets, and run cluster checks. Consumer sessions, prod connections and LLM notes are included.

cluster.noController.title: No active controller
cluster.noController.details: The cluster reports no controller: topic changes, leader elections and other metadata operations stop until a controller is elected.
cluster.noController.fix: Check the controller quorum (KRaft) or ZooKeeper and the broker logs.

partition.offline.title: Offline partitions in {{name}}
partition.offline.details: Partitions without a leader cannot be read or written: {{partitions}} ({{count}} in total).
partition.offline.fix: Bring back the brokers that hold their replicas and check the broker logs.

partition.underReplicated.title: Under-replicated partitions in {{name}}
partition.underReplicated.details: These partitions have fewer in-sync replicas than replicas: {{partitions}} ({{count}} in total).
partition.underReplicated.fix: Check that all brokers are running and keep up with replication: disks, network, load.

cluster.singleBroker.title: Single-broker cluster
cluster.singleBroker.details: There is nowhere to replicate data, and a restart or failure of the broker makes every partition unavailable.
cluster.singleBroker.fix: Use at least three brokers for stage and prod.

broker.leaderSkew.title: Leader skew on broker {{name}}
broker.leaderSkew.details: Partitions led by this broker: {{leaders}}, average per broker: {{average}} ({{deviation}}). The load on brokers is uneven.
broker.leaderSkew.fix: Run a preferred leader election or reassign partitions; check auto.leader.rebalance.enable.

partition.notPreferredLeader.title: Leaders not on the preferred replica
partition.notPreferredLeader.details: Partitions whose leader is not the first replica: {{count}}, for example {{examples}}. This usually remains after broker restarts.
partition.notPreferredLeader.fix: Run a preferred leader election or enable auto.leader.rebalance.enable.

topic.replicationFactorOne.title: Replication factor 1 for {{name}}
topic.replicationFactorOne.details: Each partition has a single replica: losing that broker loses the data and makes the partitions unavailable.
topic.replicationFactorOne.fix: Increase the replication factor to 3 by reassigning the partitions.

topic.minIsrUnreachable.title: min.insync.replicas is above the replication factor for {{name}}
topic.minIsrUnreachable.details: min.insync.replicas = {{minIsr}} ({{source}}) with replication factor {{replicationFactor}}: producers with acks=all can never write.
topic.minIsrUnreachable.fix: Set min.insync.replicas below the replication factor or increase the replication factor.

topic.minIsrEqualsRf.title: min.insync.replicas equals the replication factor for {{name}}
topic.minIsrEqualsRf.details: min.insync.replicas = {{minIsr}} ({{source}}) with replication factor {{replicationFactor}}: if one replica fails, writes with acks=all stop.
topic.minIsrEqualsRf.fix: Set min.insync.replicas one below the replication factor, for example 2 with factor 3.

topic.minIsrOne.title: min.insync.replicas is 1 for {{name}}
topic.minIsrOne.details: min.insync.replicas = 1 ({{source}}) with replication factor {{replicationFactor}}: one replica confirms an acks=all write, so a broker failure can lose confirmed messages.

topic.uncleanElection.title: Unclean leader election is allowed for {{name}}
topic.uncleanElection.details: unclean.leader.election.enable = true ({{source}}): an out-of-sync replica can become the leader, and confirmed messages can be lost.
topic.uncleanElection.fix: Set unclean.leader.election.enable = false unless availability matters more than data.

broker.autoCreateTopics.title: Brokers create topics automatically
broker.autoCreateTopics.details: auto.create.topics.enable = true (broker {{brokerId}}): a typo in a topic name creates a new topic with default settings.
broker.autoCreateTopics.fix: Set auto.create.topics.enable = false and create topics explicitly.

broker.defaultReplicationFactorOne.title: Default replication factor is 1
broker.defaultReplicationFactorOne.details: default.replication.factor = 1 (broker {{brokerId}}), brokers in the cluster: {{brokers}}. Topics created without an explicit factor get a single replica, with no redundancy.

broker.defaultMinIsrOne.title: Default min.insync.replicas is 1
broker.defaultMinIsrOne.details: min.insync.replicas = 1 (broker {{brokerId}}), brokers in the cluster: {{brokers}}. Topics without their own value confirm acks=all writes with one replica.

broker.configDrift.title: {{config}} differs between brokers
broker.configDrift.details: Values by broker: {{values}}. The cluster behaves differently depending on which broker leads a partition.
broker.configDrift.fix: Set the same value on all brokers.

group.abandoned.title: Group {{name}} is empty but has lag
group.abandoned.details: The group has no members; unread messages: {{lag}}.
group.abandoned.fix: If the application is retired, delete the group; otherwise start its consumers.

group.rebalancing.title: Group {{name}} is rebalancing
group.rebalancing.details: At the moment of the check the group is in state {{state}}.
group.rebalancing.fix: If rebalances repeat, ask the LLM assistant to observe the group, or check the consumer logs and timeouts.

group.idleMembers.title: Members without partitions in {{name}}
group.idleMembers.details: Members without partitions: {{idle}} of {{members}}; partitions assigned: {{partitions}}. There are more members than partitions.
group.idleMembers.fix: Reduce the number of consumers or add partitions to the topic.

group.lagGrowing.title: Lag of group {{name}} is growing
group.lagGrowing.details: The lag grew from {{previousLag}} to {{lag}} since the check {{minutesAgo}} min ago: the consumers do not keep up.
group.lagGrowing.fix: Check that the consumers are running and fast enough; add consumers or partitions if needed.

check.partial.title: The check is incomplete
check.partial.details: Topic configs checked: {{topicsChecked}} of {{topicsTotal}}; groups: {{groupsChecked}} of {{groupsTotal}}; read errors: {{errors}}.
check.partial.fix: Findings cover only what was read. A check reads up to 2000 topics and 500 groups within 45 seconds; if the cluster was slow, retry later.

cluster.controllerUnknown.title: Controller unknown
cluster.controllerUnknown.details: Glafira could not learn the controller id in time, but every partition has a leader, so the cluster is probably healthy.
cluster.controllerUnknown.fix: Repeat the check. If the controller stays unknown, check the controller quorum (KRaft) or ZooKeeper.

connections.environment: Marks the connection with a color. prod connections ask you to type the connection name before any change.
connections.readOnly: Blocks everything that changes the cluster: sending, offset resets, deleting topics and groups, consumer sessions.
connections.llmAccess: What an LLM assistant connected over MCP can read here. Metadata only: brokers, topics, configs, consumer groups. Metadata and messages: also masked message contents and group commits. No passwords.
connections.bootstrap: One or more host:port, comma-separated. The client discovers the other brokers by itself.
connections.protocol: PLAINTEXT — no encryption or login. SSL — TLS encryption. SASL_* — login with a password; SASL_SSL also encrypts.
connections.saslMechanism: Your Kafka admins know which one the cluster uses. SCRAM never sends the password itself; PLAIN without TLS sends it in clear text.
connections.timeout: How long to wait for a broker response, in milliseconds. Increase it for slow networks and VPNs.
connections.props: Any librdkafka setting as key=value, one per line. Passwords and keys are not allowed here.
connections.test: Checks the settings, DNS and TCP, then Kafka (TLS, SASL, metadata). Nothing is saved or changed.
connections.ca: The CA that signed the brokers' certificates. Leave empty if the system already trusts it.
connections.caFormat: File format: PEM (text, -----BEGIN), PKCS#12 (.p12, .pfx) or JKS (Java keystore).
connections.verifyHostname: Checks that the broker certificate matches its host name. Turn it off only in test environments.
connections.mtls: Needed if the brokers authenticate clients by certificate. Your Kafka admins issue the certificate and key.
connections.alias: The key entry name in the JKS or PKCS#12 file. Needed only if the file holds several keys.
connections.keyPassword: Only if the key has its own password: different from the keystore password, or an encrypted PEM key.
connections.mask: Values of JSON fields, headers and name=value pairs with these names are replaced with ***. Case and the characters _, - and . do not matter; * matches any characters.

topics.partitions: Partitions are read in parallel; order is guaranteed only within one partition. The count can be increased later but never decreased.
topics.rf: How many copies of each partition the brokers keep. At most the number of brokers; 3 is the usual choice for prod.
topics.preset: delete removes old messages by time, compact keeps the latest value per key, compact + delete does both, test keeps messages for 1 hour.
topics.extraConfigs: Any topic setting as key=value, one per line, for example retention.ms=86400000. Overrides the preset.
topics.config: “reset to default” removes the override, and the broker default applies. Nothing changes until you review and confirm the changes.

groups.strategyEarliest: The group will reread everything the topic still keeps.
groups.strategyLatest: The group skips everything accumulated and starts with new messages.
groups.strategyTimestamp: Each partition moves to the first message written at or after the given time.
groups.strategyOffset: Sets the exact offset for every selected partition.
groups.strategyShift: Moves the current offset: −N rereads N messages back, +N skips N messages.
groups.scope: Whole group, selected topics, or specific partitions as topic:partition.
groups.onlyEmpty: Active members would overwrite the new offsets with their own commits. Stop the group's applications first.
groups.preview: Shows current and new offsets per partition. Nothing changes until you apply.
groups.lag: How many messages the group has not read yet: the end of the log minus the committed offset.

browse.startPosition: Where to start reading: the latest N messages, from the beginning, from an offset, from a point in time, or the last X minutes.
browse.limit: How many messages to show. Large values make reading slower.
browse.format: How to decode keys and values: string, JSON, hex or base64. Only the display changes, not the data.
browse.readerNotGroup: Browsing does not join a consumer group and commits nothing, so the cluster is not changed.

producer.partition: Leave empty to let Kafka choose the partition by key. Enter a number to send to a specific partition.
producer.formats: Text encoding: string as is, JSON (validated), hex or base64 for binary data, null for none. The key defaults to null: with an empty string key, all messages go to one partition.
producer.placeholders: Placeholders are replaced on every send: a new UUID, the current time, the copy number and so on.
producer.acks: How many replicas must confirm a write. all is the safest, 1 is faster, 0 does not wait and messages can be lost.
producer.compression: Compresses batches: less traffic and disk space, a bit more CPU. zstd and lz4 are common choices.
producer.idempotence: Prevents duplicates when the client retries a send. Requires acks = all.
producer.batchRate: Limits batch sending to N messages per second so the cluster is not overloaded.

consumer.join: Unlike browsing, a session is a real group member: the group rebalances, and commits change its offsets.
consumer.autoCommit: Commits read offsets automatically in the background. Without it, commit manually with the commit buttons.
consumer.commit: “Commit up to selected” commits the offset after the selected message; “Commit everything read” commits all messages read so far.
consumer.pause: Pausing stops reading a partition without leaving the group, so no rebalance happens.

topicConfig.cleanup_policy: delete removes old segments by time or size, compact keeps only the latest value per key, compact,delete does both.
topicConfig.retention_ms: How long messages are kept, in ms. Default 604800000 (7 days); -1 keeps them forever. Applies when cleanup.policy includes delete.
topicConfig.retention_bytes: Maximum size of each partition before old segments are deleted. Default -1: no size limit, only time.
topicConfig.delete_retention_ms: How long delete markers (null values) stay in a compacted topic so that readers can see the deletion. Default 1 day.
topicConfig.min_compaction_lag_ms: The minimum age of a message before compaction may remove it. Default 0.
topicConfig.max_compaction_lag_ms: The maximum time a message may stay uncompacted, to guarantee that old values are removed in time. Default: unlimited.
topicConfig.min_cleanable_dirty_ratio: Compaction starts when this share of the log is uncompacted. Lower means more frequent compaction and fewer duplicates, but more disk load. Default 0.5.
topicConfig.segment_ms: How often a new log segment is started, even if the current one is not full. Retention and compaction work on whole segments. Default 7 days.
topicConfig.segment_bytes: Size of one log segment file. Retention and compaction work on whole segments. Default 1 GiB.
topicConfig.segment_jitter_ms: Up to this much random time is subtracted from segment.ms, so that many partitions do not start new segments at the same moment. Default 0.
topicConfig.file_delete_delay_ms: How long a deleted segment file stays on disk before it is actually removed. Default 1 minute.
topicConfig.local_retention_ms: With tiered storage: how long segments stay on the broker's local disk before only the remote copy remains. -2 means the same as retention.ms.
topicConfig.local_retention_bytes: With tiered storage: local size limit per partition; older segments remain only in remote storage. -2 means the same as retention.bytes.
topicConfig.remote_storage_enable: Enables tiered storage: closed segments are copied to remote storage (for example, S3) and later removed locally. The cluster must support it.
topicConfig.remote_log_copy_disable: Stops copying new segments to remote storage; data already there stays readable. Used to turn tiered storage off step by step.
topicConfig.remote_log_delete_on_disable: When tiered storage is turned off for the topic, delete its data in remote storage. Must be true to turn tiered storage off.
topicConfig.compression_type: How the broker stores messages: producer keeps the producer's compression; otherwise it stores them as gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd or uncompressed, recompressing if needed.
topicConfig.compression_gzip_level: gzip level when the broker recompresses to gzip: 1 is the fastest, 9 the smallest. Kafka 3.8+.
topicConfig.compression_lz4_level: lz4 level when the broker recompresses to lz4: higher is smaller and slower. Kafka 3.8+.
topicConfig.compression_zstd_level: zstd level when the broker recompresses to zstd: higher is smaller and slower. Kafka 3.8+.
topicConfig.max_message_bytes: Largest batch the broker accepts for this topic; larger messages are rejected. Producers must allow the same size (max.request.size). Default about 1 MB.
topicConfig.min_insync_replicas: How many replicas must confirm a write with acks=all, otherwise the producer gets an error. Usually 2 with replication factor 3.
topicConfig.unclean_leader_election_enable: Lets an out-of-sync replica become leader when no in-sync replica is left. The topic stays available, but messages may be lost.
topicConfig.message_timestamp_type: CreateTime: the timestamp set by the producer. LogAppendTime: the time the broker wrote the message.
topicConfig.message_timestamp_before_max_ms: How far in the past a producer timestamp may be with CreateTime; older messages are rejected.
topicConfig.message_timestamp_after_max_ms: How far in the future a producer timestamp may be with CreateTime; messages beyond it are rejected.
topicConfig.message_timestamp_difference_max_ms: Deprecated, replaced by the two message.timestamp.*.max.ms settings: the allowed gap between producer and broker time. Removed in Kafka 4.0.
topicConfig.message_format_version: Deprecated: the message format for old clients. Ignored since Kafka 3.0 and removed in 4.0.
topicConfig.message_downconversion_enable: Lets the broker convert messages for very old consumers; costs CPU. Has no effect since Kafka 4.0 (deprecated).
topicConfig.flush_messages: Force a disk flush every N messages. Usually left at the default: Kafka relies on replication and the OS page cache.
topicConfig.flush_ms: Force a disk flush every N milliseconds. Usually left at the default: Kafka relies on replication and the OS page cache.
topicConfig.index_interval_bytes: How often an offset index entry is written, in bytes of log. Smaller means faster seeks but a larger index. Rarely changed.
topicConfig.segment_index_bytes: Maximum size of a segment's offset index file. Rarely changed.
topicConfig.preallocate: Preallocate the segment file on disk when it is created. May help on some file systems; rarely changed.
topicConfig.leader_replication_throttled_replicas: Replicas whose replication is throttled on the leader side, as partition:broker or *. Set by reassignment tools; usually not edited by hand.
topicConfig.follower_replication_throttled_replicas: Replicas whose replication is throttled on the follower side, as partition:broker or *. Set by reassignment tools; usually not edited by hand.

import.target: Where new folders and connections go. Existing ones stay where they are.
import.updateExisting: Connections that already exist get the settings from the file; your passwords and their place in the tree are kept.

settings.mcpEnable: Starts a local MCP server for LLM assistants. Access is opened per connection and is off by default; each new client is confirmed in a dialog.

health.check: Runs Glafira’s built-in rules: partitions and replication, topic and broker configs, consumer groups. Severity depends on the connection environment. The check only reads the cluster.
health.hidden: Findings you hid for a specific object. They do not count in badges; LLM assistants see them marked as hidden.
health.proposals: A change an LLM assistant suggests. Nothing is applied until you open it in a form and confirm; you can edit the values first.
